newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip, nervously eye U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip, nervously eye U.S. inflation.

text.p: Argentine bonds were a tad lower late Wednesday after a dull session shadowing the movements of U.S. Treasuries.

"The market was without flows, apathetic - there is not much to comment today," said a trader at a foreign bank. That calm underlined the overwhelming uncertainty hanging over the market on the direction of U.S. rates.
If Friday's U.S. inflation report comes in on the high side, Argentine bonds will suffer with the U.S. market as another U.S. rate hike will be priced into the market, traders said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 fell 1/8 to 89-5/8.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.02 to 128.00.
In spite of supportive domestic fundamentals, "we cannot separate ourselves from the U.S. market," said another trader.
Traders predicted the market would tread water on Thursday as well before Friday's decisive report.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.83 percent from 5.88 percent.
